newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's prime minister to Egypt for Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's prime minister to Egypt for Hebron talks.

text.p: Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti flew to Cairo on Monday for talks with President Hosni Mubarak to help promote a compromise deal on Palestinian self-rule in the volatile West Bank town of Hebron.

A Jordanian official said Kabariti, who accompanied King Hussein's surprise mediation mission to Gaza and Tel Aviv, would "coordinate with the Egyptians to keep the ball rolling" after the two sides moved closer to an accord on Sunday.

Palestinian and Israeli negotiators were due to meet in Jerusalem to draft final points in the agreement, including a compromise reached on Sunday for the completion of three Israeli troop withdrawals from rural West Bank areas by mid-1998.

A timeframe for the pullbacks, originally scheduled to be completed by September this year, has been the main stumbling block to sealing a deal on implementing a long overdue Israeli troop redeployment from Hebron.
King Hussein discussed the mid-1998 compromise during talks on Sunday in Gaza with Arafat and by telephone with Mubarak before flying to Tel Aviv to see Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
